sections.title: Canonical expandable Work layout
blocks: Each work folder has one index.yaml node; index is the node, not an extra directory listing.

Split by responsibility as needed: business, architecture, backend, frontend and uat each own nodes. Business can split into rules, journeys and acceptance; FE into draw/code; UAT into flows. Names and depth are flexible, not mandatory scaffolding.
A leaf has requirements, assertions and state. A parent keeps scope and derives progress from required children, never authored state/completion.

Extend existing nodes and preserve stable IDs, assets and evidence. New required work prevents parent done; unrelated completed branches remain intact. Scope or source changes invalidate only affected proof.
Several workflows may target the same work nodes; no duplicated business tree per run. Local workflow tracking is ignored by validation/digests and Git.
Declare semantic design/source files using node.assets with paths under own assets/. Their actual bytes contribute to node input binding.

Record output screenshots/videos in evidence assets with scope: node and paths under the primary owner assets/. Output evidence is not also declared as a semantic input, avoiding self-invalidating proof.
Source code remains in bound repositories; code/index.yaml tracks requirements, exact source references and completion.
Legacy node.yaml/node.md remains read compatibility; exactly one node file per work folder. Do not automatically migrate existing user work.

sections.title: Read-only Work metadata core
blocks: `validateWorkspace(root)` is synchronous and returns `{ok,errors,warnings,nodes,resources}`. Each diagnostic has `code,path,message`; paths are workspace-relative. Node summaries expose `id,path,kind,required,state,effectiveState,specDigest,inputDigest,eligible,children,dependsOn,refs,blockedBy,suspensionReasons`. `dependsOn` and `refs` contain safe, unique sorted effective IDs (own plus inherited scope); `blockedBy` lists direct effective prerequisites not currently done. `suspensionReasons` contains `{code,ids}` with `INPUT_CHANGED`, `PREREQUISITE_NOT_DONE`, `CHILD_SUSPENDED` or `DECLARED_SUSPENSION`. Resources expose only `id,path,kind,revision,specDigest`. No metadata bodies, account details, raw file bytes or credentials are printed. Unknown extension data stays untouched on disk and participates in semantic hashes. `canonicalJSON(value)`, `sha256(bytesOrString)`, `profiles` and `impactWorkspace(root,id)` are also exported.

Metadata uses YAML 1.2. node.yaml contains schema/id/kind/required, description text, declared assertions and dependencies; state/completion are validated. Duplicate keys, custom tags and aliases are rejected. Unknown reserved fields are errors; namespaced extensions and resource.details remain data. YAML schema output lives under .work/_schema and uses the same source shape as the core.

sections.title: Layout and identity
blocks: The argument is the `.work` directory, containing `workspace.yaml`. Resources live under `_resources/**/resource.yaml`. Arbitrary business directories contain `index.yaml`; the nearest ancestor node defines the parent. A parent cannot store state or completion. Evidence uses `evidence/<id>/manifest.yaml` under a node or business directory, referenced by stable metadata ID. Global IDs are unique across workspace, nodes, resources and evidence; directory names are not IDs. Intermediate folders without nodes are permitted. `evidence`, `assets` and `_resources` are reserved artifact/resource directory roles: a `index.yaml` or legacy `node.md` anywhere below them is rejected and never enters the completion tree. `_local`, `_workflows`, `_schema` and `.git` are ignored. Canonical symlinks and path traversal are rejected; secrets stay outside this root, referenced by sealed provider aliases in resource details. Known plaintext credential fields are rejected recursively in every metadata type, including workspace extensions. This is a conservative key check, not comprehensive secret detection in arbitrary prose or disguised values. The validator does not fetch remote assets or resolve secrets.

sections.title: Digests and effective state
blocks: `specDigest` covers all node metadata except fields marked `x-operational` in the schema (`state`, `completion`, `blocker`, `suspensionReason`, `timestamps`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`), plus normalized Markdown body. `naReason` is semantic: changing an applicability justification invalidates consumers of that scope. Unknown extension fields are included conservatively. `inputDigest` additionally binds workspace metadata, ancestor specifications and their referenced inputs, recursively referenced nodes/dependencies/resources, and descendants for branches. An inherited ancestor `refs` entry pointing at the current node or its containing subtree is redundant and is not recursively expanded; this permits a goal to reference its requirements subtree without making that subtree inherit a false reference to itself. Explicit references and all dependency edges still undergo cycle detection. Node paths are excluded so a rename preserving hierarchy and IDs does not invalidate proof. Resource metadata, including its explicit revision and details, is bound in full. Resource-to-resource links inside arbitrary details are not interpreted; reference every applicable resource from the consuming node. No field hidden inside extension prose is automatically a dependency.

Changing only completion or state does not mechanically alter a digest. Dependency eligibility is still checked separately: a consumer requires its own and inherited ancestor `dependsOn` targets to be effectively **done**. An N/A prerequisite does not prove a module/account/service exists. `refs` bind semantic inputs but do not impose an execution gate. A changed specification/resource yields effective `suspended` and retained `STALE_COMPLETION`/`STALE_EVIDENCE` diagnostics until actual re-verification; never overwrite a digest merely to clear the gate. A previously done consumer whose prerequisite regresses also becomes suspended, even if its input digest is unchanged. Persisted `state:done` and its evidence remain intact; validation never writes a replacement status. Todo/doing consumers with unmet prerequisites retain their declared state but expose `eligible:false` and `blockedBy`. Restoring the exact prerequisite can restore validity only when all original input/evidence bindings still match; changed semantics require fresh verification.

Declared leaf states: `todo`, `doing`, `blocked`, `done`, `na`, `suspended`. Effective state additionally includes `invalid`. Authored `suspended` requires a nonempty concrete `suspensionReason`; it represents imported or explicitly unverified scope, requires no fabricated previous completion/evidence, and never satisfies a prerequisite or contributes done. In particular, a business inferred from code is an observation awaiting owner approval, not an approved requirement. `suspensionReason` is operational and changing it alone does not alter semantic digests. This authored state differs from derived suspended: when recorded done loses current input/prerequisite validity, the validator retains the original done/evidence on disk and only reports suspended in its output. Do not rewrite historical proof into an import record.

N/A requires a reason and is not evidence of passing. Required children drive parent rollup; all N/A becomes N/A, mixed done/N/A becomes done, otherwise invalid/blocked/suspended/doing/todo applies. This completion rollup does not make an N/A prerequisite pass its separate dependency gate. An all-optional branch is N/A, not certified done; unfinished optional work produces a warning. Shared metadata/evidence integrity errors fail closed for all nodes. Unknown leaf kinds remain readable with warnings but cannot earn `done`; supported profiles must be implemented and tested before certifying new kinds.

Resources may declare `files:[{path}]`. Each path is normalized and relative to the directory containing that resource's `resource.yaml`; paths cannot escape it, use symlinks, point to a directory or require remote retrieval. The core hashes actual local file bytes at validation time and incorporates their normalized paths and computed SHA-256 into the resource specification digest. No authored hash field is required. A linked design-image edit therefore suspends its UI consumers without needing a manual resource revision bump. Transitive consumers are invalidated through declared refs/dependencies; a valid edit to an unreferenced resource does not invalidate unrelated leaves. File integrity checks do not interpret the design's meaning or automatically inspect external code/runtime.

sections.title: Read-only impact inspection
blocks: `impactWorkspace(root,id)` returns `{ok,errors,warnings,target,affected}`. Target is `{id,path,type:"node"|"resource"}` or null with `MISSING_TARGET`; affected entries are `{id,path,kind,direct,via:[id],reasons:[reason]}` and exclude the source itself. Reasons are `dependency`, `reference`, `ancestor-spec` and `child-input`. `ok` and diagnostics reflect current workspace validation, so suspended proof can be inspected even while validation reports failures.

Impact means the declared graph potentially consumes a changed source specification or resource bytes; it is not a command to execute. A node specification change affects its descendants through inherited scope. An input change propagates to explicit/effective consumers and parent rollups, but **parent input alone never propagates back into an unrelated sibling**. The `child-input` reason denotes derived parent rollup, not a new parent implementation op. This distinction avoids a design-image edit selecting unrelated backend work. No automatic task, op, rerun or file mutation occurs.

sections.title: Completion profiles
blocks: Every supported done leaf declares nonempty `assertions:[id]`. Completion is `{inputDigest,evidence:[evidenceId],codeRefs?:[{repository,commit}]}`. Evidence must explicitly bind that node and its current inputs, report overall pass, contain nonempty passing observations, and cover every declared assertion ID. A failed, missing, not-run or inconclusive assertion cannot become done. Hashes establish binding and byte integrity, **not the truth of an observation**.

One run bundle can serve multiple leaves without copying screenshots: retain its primary `nodeId,inputDigest`, then add `bindings:[{nodeId,inputDigest}]` for additional consumers. Every bound node ID must resolve and appear only once (including the primary); each consumer is checked against its own current digest and declared assertions. Store the manifest and assets once at the flow's `evidence/<id>/` and reference the same evidence ID from each appropriate leaf. An unlisted consumer cannot reuse the proof. Changing one consumer suspends that consumer, not an unrelated binding whose inputs still match. Overall failure or corrupted assets invalidates the shared bundle for all consumers.

Implementation and release require repository resource IDs and full lowercase 40/64-hex commit SHAs. Those resource IDs must be in node `refs`; every selected evidence record must carry corresponding `codeRefs`. The core does not check Git object existence, ancestry, remote publication or commit origin. Record original versus integrated commits in explicit extensions when required; do not equate one commit binding with deployed code.

Operators must refresh applicable repository and environment resource revisions from actual inspected code/build state before validation. The core re-hashes explicitly declared local resource files, but does not otherwise watch repository source files or deployments. A changed Git HEAD or remote runtime is not automatically detected if applicable metadata is left unchanged; hashes cannot repair stale or fabricated inputs. `eligible` means structurally valid with satisfied own/inherited prerequisites, not user approval or authority to execute.

UAT evidence requires `provenance:{environment,actor,servedVersions,tool,capturedAt,servedVersionEvidence}` or `anonymous:true` instead of actor. Environment and actor resolve to resources of kinds `environment` and `identity`. Each served version is `{repository,commit,artifact}`: an actual observed immutable image/build identity, not a copied source HEAD. `servedVersionEvidence` identifies a passing assertion explaining the runtime version observation. Environment, actor and repository IDs must be included in node refs for invalidation. The core verifies declared binding, not the external endpoint; an operator must inspect the actual served target and capture tool-derived observations. A fabricated build label can pass structural checks and must be caught by tool evidence and review.

`uat.ui` additionally requires hashed local PNG/JPEG/WebP image bytes. Image recognition checks file signatures only, not complete image decoding, correct rendering, authenticity, viewport or freshness. The operator must open and examine the image. `uat.ux` requires at least one passing assertion marked `kind:"behavior"`; screenshot-only evidence cannot suffice. Observation semantics and assertion adequacy require review.

Evidence assets are relative normalized paths under their evidence directory with SHA-256; missing files, mismatched hashes, absolute paths, traversal and symlinks are rejected. Remote-only evidence cannot be certified in this implementation. No command runs, no account is created, no state is repaired and no next op is dispatched by validation.

sections.title: Minimal authoring sequence
blocks: Author source requirements/resources and a `todo` leaf with declared assertions. Call validation to obtain its current `inputDigest`. Execute only the approved op, save real evidence with that digest and actual code/runtime binding. Set completion only after reviewing passing proof; revalidate. These steps are operator responsibilities, not an automatic chain. Examples and tests use synthetic observations and must not be cited as product acceptance.

Structured `extensions.work3.specification` is validated through `specifications/contract.json`: coverage/IDs, source revision bindings, receiving-service ownership, pattern mechanisms and threat review. Canonical `journeys` use the same validator as the FE workflow. Referenced business journey changes in architecture produce `SPECIFICATION_JOURNEY_DRIFT`. This is structure and binding validation, not proof of deployed behavior or approved intent.
